narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Warm and mostly sunny conditions will dominate Kisumu today, with a slight chance of isolated late afternoon or early evening light showers as the lake breeze develops. Temperatures will reach a high near 29°C / 84°F before settling to a cool low of 16°C / 61°F overnight, maintaining a consistent equatorial late-dry-season pattern.

## Today's Forecast
Daytime conditions across Kisumu and the surrounding Nyanza lowlands will feature sun mixed with afternoon cloudiness. High temperatures will peak around 29°C / 84°F, dropping to an overnight low around 16°C / 61°F. Light isolated showers may develop between 16:00 EAT and 20:00 EAT, though rainfall accumulations will remain negligible at 0.1 mm (0.00 in) to 0.9 mm (0.04 in). Winds will shift from morning easterlies to an afternoon lake breeze of 21 km/h (11 kt) from the SW, with evening gusts reaching up to 37 km/h (20 kt). Solar radiation will be intense with a peak UV index of 8.8 (Very High). Air quality is Moderate, with the ground sensor at Kisumu International Airport recording an AQI of 84 (PM2.5 84.0 µg/m³), which aligns with model predictions (CAMS US AQI 73–82).

## Extended Outlook
The near-term period (Days 1–3, Wednesday through Friday) will remain predominantly warm and dry across the Nyanza Basin. Daytime highs will climb into the 30°C / 86°F to 32°C / 90°F range, under gentle to moderate daytime breezes. Rainfall potential remains near zero through Friday, August 14.

Looking ahead to the extended range (Days 4–7, Saturday through Tuesday), model guidance indicates a transition toward enhanced moisture and instability by Sunday, August 17 and Monday, August 18. Temperatures will drop to around 26°C / 79°F to 28°C / 82°F under increasing cloud cover. Widespread scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected, with daily rainfall sums reaching 2.7 mm (0.11 in) to 6.3 mm (0.25 in). Consult Day+3 and Day+7 model performance metrics when assessing confidence in this transition window.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe weather hazards are anticipated for today. Isolated evening shower activity carries minimal threat of heavy accumulation or severe lightning. However, localized wind gusts up to 37 km/h (20 kt) associated with lake breeze convergence may briefly produce choppy conditions along the shore. Stronger lacustrine winds are projected for Friday, August 14, where open-lake gusts could approach 47 km/h (25 kt).

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Over open waters in the northeastern sector of Lake Victoria, morning winds will blow at 19 km/h (10 kt) from the SE, shifting to 15 km/h (8 kt) from the WNW during the late afternoon. Peak surface winds will reach 19 km/h (10 kt) with isolated gusts up to 27 km/h (15 kt). Wave heights are expected to remain manageable at 0.3 m to 0.6 m (1.0 ft to 2.0 ft). Boaters should remain alert for localized wind shifts during the late afternoon lake-breeze transition.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Mean sea-level pressure across the Nyanza Basin remains steady around 1013 hPa to 1015 hPa, governed by a weak equatorial pressure trough and stable continental air masses to the east. Diurnal surface heating combined with differential heating between Lake Victoria and the adjacent landmass will drive the development of a classic lake-breeze front this afternoon. Atmospheric moisture remains relatively shallow, limiting CAPE values over land (300–800 J/kg) and keeping convective activity limited to weak, short-lived isolated showers. Pressure trends over the next 24 to 72 hours across regional basin stations (Busia, Homa Bay, Migori, Kisii) remain flat to slightly rising (1013 hPa to 1017 hPa), maintaining suppression of widespread synoptic convection until late weekend.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Forecast confidence for the immediate 24-to-72-hour period is high due to strong model agreement between ECMWF, GFS, ICON, and UKMO regarding low rainfall accumulation and seasonal temperatures. As no historical verification scores or rolling accuracy checks are available yet for this initial run, model weights are distributed evenly, relying on live METAR observations from Kisumu Airport (HKKI 111130Z) for surface truth. Confidence decreases slightly for the Day 5–7 period regarding the exact onset timing and accumulation of the late-weekend precipitation signal.
